A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and three algorithms. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and matchable despite reformatting.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices F–G report original synthetic optimization, ResNet-18/CIFAR-10, logistic regression, and stepsize-sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: The same original experimental results remain in Section 5 and Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain their update rules, clipping locations, aggregation, and reshuffling procedures. CLERR-h and practical pseudogradient variants already appear in v1. The revised sufficient stepsize bounds concern the convergence analysis.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate shifted quartic objectives, CIFAR-10 image classification, and logistic regression on gisette and realsim. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SO, Nastya, and CSO for CLERR; CELGC and CE-FedAvg for Clip-LocalGDJ; and CE-FedAvg-PP for Clipped RR-CLI. Appendix G.2 retains the CLERR–CSO comparison. The newly cited Crawshaw work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and F–G retain the data construction, client and cohort sizes, batch sizes, metrics, and hyperparameter-selection procedures. Tables 1–7 preserve the same search grids. The theoretical stepsize correction does not change the reported experimental settings.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the local-step and starting-point comparisons, CLERR-h investigation, and Appendix G.1 inner-stepsize sensitivity study. Their questions and supporting analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report 10 seeds for the synthetic comparisons and three for the CIFAR-10 and logistic regression experiments. The averaging descriptions and plotted uncertainty bands remain unchanged; no statistical reporting procedure is added.

E6.justification: Figures 1–10 reuse identical plot images, including their curves and numerical labels. The accompanying experimental findings, including CLERR's synthetic advantage and the strong CIFAR-10 performance of CSO, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and Appendix B correct substantive local-step accumulation errors. Lemma 4's dependence changes from (v_p−t_p)^2 to (v_p−t_p)^3; Lemma 5 also changes its prefactor from 16 to 32. Theorems 1 and 5 replace H−1 with (H−1)^2, with corresponding corrections to corollaries and PŁ stepsize conditions. These alter the guarantees' dependence on local steps while retaining the headline epoch complexities.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the assertion that no partial-participation results exist under generalized smoothness with acknowledgment of one earlier result without data shuffling. This narrows the novelty rationale, although Section 1.1 retains its broad 'first result' claim. The other central contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of clipping, jumping, client drift, and experimental behavior are retained. The discussion of excessively small or large inner stepsizes and the future-work boundaries in Section 6 are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F replaces the anonymous code-access link with a named GitHub repository link. The experimental implementation descriptions and hyperparameter grids remain unchanged. Repository availability was not checked externally.

R1.justification: V2 adds Crawshaw et al. (2024a), distinguishing its partial-participation analysis by its heterogeneity assumptions and lack of reshuffling. It removes the sentence summarizing Gorbunov et al. (2024), while retaining that reference. Other added main-text citations already appeared in v1's Appendix H.

P1.justification: The narrative and section sequence are largely retained, with limited introduction and related-work edits, revised affiliations, and expanded acknowledgements. The main-text pseudogradient explanation is removed but remains covered in Appendices E–F. Section 5.1.1's valid appendix reference becomes 'Appendix ??'.

P2.justification: The ICLR template changes the title, headers, text width, and heading styles, with resized plots and relocated algorithms and tables. Figure 4 becomes a text-wrapped side figure. All ten figures and seven tables retain their display content and organization.

improvement.justification: The corrected local-step factors and stepsize conditions improve the accuracy of the existing theory, and the Crawshaw citation improves attribution. The gain is limited: Appendix E still uses the earlier Lemma 4-based factor, Section 1.1 retains the broad novelty claim, and Section 5.1.1 introduces a broken reference. The algorithms and empirical support remain unchanged.
